{"retrieved_sources": {"BRD-K56343971": [{"source_id": "pubchem:42611257:description:1", "text": "Vemurafenib is a pyrrolopyridine that is 1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine which is substituted at position 5 by a p-chlorophenyl group and at positions 3 by a 3-amino-2,6-difluorobenzoyl group, the amino group of which has undergone formal condensation with propane-1-sulfonic acid to give the corresponding sulfonamide. An inhibitor of BRAF and other kinases. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a B-Raf inhibitor. It is a sulfonamide, a difluorobenzene, a pyrrolopyridine, an aromatic ketone and a member of monochlorobenzenes.", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:63637"}], "BRD-K12502280": [{"source_id": "pubchem:16722836:description:1", "text": "N-tert-butyl-3-[[5-methyl-2-[4-[2-(1-pyrrolidinyl)ethoxy]anilino]-4-pyrimidinyl]amino]benzenesulfonamide is a sulfonamide.", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:91408"}], "BRD-K13662825": [{"source_id": "pubchem:46926350:description:1", "text": "Dinaciclib is a pyrazolopyrimidine that is pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine substituted by ethyl, (2S)-2-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperidin-1-yl, and [(1-oxidopyridin-3-yl)methyl]amino groups at positions 3, 5, and 7, respectively. It is a potent pan-cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor that exhibits antineoplastic activity. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, an apoptosis inducer and an EC 2.7.11.22 (cyclin-dependent kinase) inhibitor. It is a primary alcohol, a member of piperidines, a member of pyridine N-oxides, a pyrazolopyrimidine, a secondary amino compound and a tertiary amino compound.", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:95060"}], "BRD-K87909389": [{"source_id": "pubchem:5287969:description:1", "text": "Alvocidib is a synthetic dihydroxyflavone that is 5,7-dihydroxyflavone which is substituted by a 3-hydroxy-1-methylpiperidin-4-yl group at position 8 and by a chlorine at the 2' position (the ()-3S,4R stereoisomer). A cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK9) inhibitor, it has been studied for the treatment of acute myeloid leukaemia, arthritis and atherosclerotic plaque formation. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, an antirheumatic drug, an apoptosis inducer and an EC 2.7.11.22 (cyclin-dependent kinase) inhibitor. It is a dihydroxyflavone, a hydroxypiperidine, a tertiary amino compound and a member of monochlorobenzenes. donors.reason: BRAF inhibitor in same MAPK pathway as MEK inhibitor selumetinib; plausible shared downstream histone effects.
Pan-CDK inhibitor; CDK inhibition can alter histone marks, overlapping observed acetylation/methylation pattern.
CDK9 inhibitor; CDK9 inhibition affects RNA Pol II and histone acetylation, matching observed marks.
Sulfonamide kinase inhibitor; limited mechanistic overlap, but high anchor similarity supports retrieval.
Amphetamine-like kinase inhibitor; weak mechanistic link, retained only for moderate anchor similarity.

revised_hypotheses: Selumetinib MEK1/2 inhibition reduces ERK signaling, indirectly lowering H3K27me3K36me0 and H3K27me2K36me1 while increasing H3K9 acetylation/methylation marks.
Selumetinib may share CDK9/CDK-mediated transcriptional effects with dinaciclib and flavopiridol, altering histone acetylation and methylation.
Selumetinib may share MAPK-pathway effects with vemurafenib, producing overlapping histone modification changes in A375 cells.
Non-MAPK kinase inhibition by TG101348 or afuresertib is less likely to explain the observed histone pattern.
unresolved: No direct evidence links selumetinib to the specific histone mark changes in A375 at 5.5 uM for 24 h.
Donor descriptions are pharmacological class information, not context-specific histone response data.
Whether the observed pattern is MEK-specific or a general kinase-inhibitor stress response remains unresolved.
